articles.title: AI Agent Incident Response: What NIST, NSA and CISA Now Expect
articles.excerpt: In one week of October 2026, four public sources described AI agents doing things nobody asked them to do. A frontier lab reported its own models working around restrictions on the live internet. Indi…
articles.body: In one week of October 2026, four public sources described AI agents doing things nobody asked them to do. A frontier lab reported its own models working around restrictions on the live internet. India's national CERT reported agents under evaluation reading confidential records on live corporate systems. The UK government said it will build ways to contain agentic AI incidents. And three US agencies published the first incident response practices written specifically for agents that act outside their instructions. None of this was a hypothetical red-team exercise. It is incident data. The question for any organization running agents is no longer whether an agent can leave its lane. It is whether you would notice, whether you could stop it, and whether you could reconstruct what it did.

articles.title: Ghostlight: Turning Personal Memories into Stories with Local AI 👻
articles.excerpt: What I Built Have you ever remembered a small moment from your past and wished you could put that feeling into words? That was the idea behind Ghostlight — Memories That Stay. Ghostlight is a small pr…
articles.body: What I Built Have you ever remembered a small moment from your past and wished you could put that feeling into words? That was the idea behind Ghostlight — Memories That Stay . Ghostlight is a small project I built to turn personal memories into written stories using local AI. You can enter a memory, choose a writing style, and let the AI help you turn it into a heartfelt letter, short story, remembrance note, or even a spooky tale. I liked the idea of connecting AI with something personal rather than using it only for coding or answering questions. Our memories are often made up of simple things—a conversation with a friend, a childhood experience, or a moment we don't want to forget. Ghostlight is my attempt to give those moments a place to stay.

After weeks of frenzied speculation, Anthropic has filed its IPO prospectus. But Anthropic has been honing its storytelling skills for years. articles.title: How an AI agent can e-file a tax return
articles.excerpt: If you've asked an AI agent to "send my return to the IRS," you've probably watched it go looking for an IRS e-file API that doesn't exist. Only Authorized IRS e-file Providers can send returns to the…
articles.body: If you've asked an AI agent to "send my return to the IRS," you've probably watched it go looking for an IRS e-file API that doesn't exist. Only Authorized IRS e-file Providers can send returns to the IRS, so an agent can't post a 1040 there directly. I built Terminal Tax (terminal.tax) to be that last step. It's a hosted MCP server at https://mcp.terminal.tax/v1/hosted-mcp . No API key or install, so any agent that can make a web request can call it. The agent sends the person's tax numbers. We calculate and check the return and send back one private link. The person opens it, reviews the return, and signs it themselves, and then we e-file it. Their SSN and signing PIN go on that page, never in the chat. The exact requests are at https://terminal.tax/llms.txt .

articles.title: What causes mysterious long delayed radio echoes in Earth's atmosphere?
articles.excerpt: Baffling long radio echo delays have prompted a range of potential explanations, most of which focus on a variety of unexplained natural phenomena occurring in Earth's atmosphere.
articles.body: In 1927, Norwegian civil engineer and amateur radio operator Jørgen Hals made an unusual discovery: while monitoring transmissions from a shortwave radio station in Eindhoven, The Netherlands, he began hearing odd, "delayed" radio echoes, arriving approximately three seconds after the original transmissions, that sometimes accompanied the station's signals. "From where this echo comes I cannot say for the present," Hals wrote of his peculiar discovery, adding that he could "only confirm that I really heard it." Almost a century after Hals' discovery, the exact cause of this unusual phenomenon — known today as long delayed echoes, or LDEs — remains unknown.

articles.title: SpaceX Falcon 9 launches early morning Starlink mission from California (video)
articles.excerpt: SpaceX launched 27 more Starlink satellites to low Earth orbit overnight (Oct. 27), aboard a Falcon 9 rocket that lifted off from California in the wee hours of darkness.
articles.body: A new stack of Starlink satellites is now in orbit following an early morning SpaceX launch from California. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off at 3:25 a.m. EDT (0725 GMT) on Oct. 27, from from Pad 4E at Vandenberg Space Force Base. The rocket delivered the 27 satellites of Starlink Group 15-16 to low Earth orbit (LEO), and successfully executed its first stage booster landing. The mission's booster, B1082, cut its engines and disengaged from Falcon 9's upper stage approximately 2.5 minutes into flight, and adjusted its trajectory for a touchdown on SpaceX's Of Course I Still Love You (OCISLY) droneship in the Pacific Ocean. A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket launches 27 Starlink satellites from California on Oct. 23, 2026.

articles.title: Astroscale proposes fleet of 'bodyguard' spacecraft to protect satellites from orbital attacks
articles.excerpt: Technologies developed to remove space junk and fix broken satellites can be repurposed to build fleets of bodyguard spacecraft to protect important assets from attacks.
articles.body: Technologies developed and tested in orbit to remove space junk and fix broken satellites can be speedily repurposed to build fleets of bodyguard spacecraft to protect important satellites from adversary attacks, space clean-up company Astroscale thinks. Astroscale made history with its 2024 up-close in-orbit inspection of a discarded Japanese rocket stage during the pioneering ADRAS-J mission in low Earth orbit (LEO), the region of space below altitudes of 1,200 miles (2,000 kilometers). The firm's ELSA-D mission , which ran from 2021 to 2024, was the first commercial endeavor to demonstrate orbital capture technologies in LEO. Now, this technology can come in handy as Western space assets face increasing threats from Russia.
articles.author: Tereza Pultarova

articles.title: How solid-state transformers could help power the AI boom
articles.excerpt: Transformers are a crucial but nearly invisible part of our grid. The devices help efficiently move power across long distances, but they’re complicated and in short supply. And given that their basic…
articles.body: Transformers are a crucial but nearly invisible part of our grid. The devices help efficiently move power across long distances, but they’re complicated and in short supply. And given that their basic design hasn’t changed much for about a century, they could use an upgrade.  As the world races to meet rising electricity demand from EVs, data centers, and more, researchers and companies are looking to modernize transformers. New, solid-state versions could help relieve some of the supply concerns and make sure the grid can handle the growing pressure. Conventional transformers generally rely on huge amounts of specialized steel alloys and miles of copper wire to do their work of transferring electricity between circuits.

articles.excerpt: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 October 27 –… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a differen…
articles.body: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 October 27 –… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Noctilucent Clouds over Sweden Explanation: Sometimes it’s night on the ground but day in the air. As the Earth rotates to eclipse the Sun, sunset rises up from the ground. Therefore, at sunset on the ground, sunlight still shines on clouds above. Under usual circumstances , a pretty sunset might be visible, but unusual noctilucent clouds float so high up they can be seen well after dark.
